items.title: Karl-Anthony Towns Embracing 'Sacrifice' After Knicks Table Extension Talks
items.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns says he remains willing to sacrifice for the New York Knicks as he chases a second straight championship. Towns has taken the fewest shots of his career this season, even though the club has put contract extension talks on hold until later in the season. Towns explained his mindset after helping the Knicks win their first title in more than 50 years. "Ever since I got here, all I've ever said is that I want to do whatever it takes to win a title," said Towns. "You win one and, you know, this year I want to do it again. I'm always willing to do whatever it takes. I've always sacrificed for the betterment of the team." Towns recorded his 10th straight double-double to open the season in Tuesday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks. Towns is on pace for career highs in shooting efficiency and rebounding. The Knicks have won four straight and six of their last seven games. Towns had publicly voiced frustration before the season that the two sides were far apart on an extension. The Knicks then announced they would not hold extension talks with eligible players until later in the season. Towns has not been offered more than $200 million. Owner James Dolan has said he does not want the team in the second apron. Towns is eligible for a four-year, $276 million extension but has said he does not expect it. Towns has said he would accept less, but still wants a salary that reflects his standing in the league and his contributions to the franchise. Towns addressed the situation at the end of training camp. "We're all humans," said Towns. "My only philosophy since we won, only thing on my mind, is how do we win another one? For me, it's the same focus I came into this season with is the same focus I'm going into Game 1 with: How do we keep the trophy in New York beyond this one summer?"
